changes.summary: Distiller durable output contract removes omission/rejection narration; meaningful unresolved conditions are represented as uncertainty while unsupported or low-value material is absent.
Evaluation diagnostics are explicitly separated from durable distiller output and must not be admitted to project memory.

repository_delta_since_prior_architect_e.finding: The distiller changes sharpen the experimental boundary between durable semantic output and evaluation diagnostics. They do not change the frozen pems/1, cove/1, or jcs/1 contracts and do not authorize canonical-memory mutation.

human_reasoning: The new distiller commits are meaningful experimental design work because they prevent omission logs and rejection explanations from leaking into durable engineering memory. That is consistent with the existing separation between governed project truth and diagnostic/evaluation material. However, the Distiller workstream remains experimental and no Steward or owner authorization opens a representation-change tranche. Canonical memory still matches production main, so promoting these experimental rules into PEMS would silently expand scope. The correct Architect result is therefore to record the delta, preserve the boundary, and make no representation change.
